I will keep my plan steady and practical. I am 73, I have farmed for 50 years, and my family has some off-farm work, so I will not chase a complicated high-input plan. I will put most of my land into the wheat-maize rotation because that is the system I know best and it fits my well irrigation. I will keep a smaller piece in cotton so I still have some cash income, but I will not expand it because cotton needs more labor and more pest watching. On the wheat-maize land, I will use better seed, put on enough fertilizer to keep yields stable, irrigate when the crop really needs it, and keep field work simple to save labor. For maize, I will use hybrid seed and lean toward less tillage after wheat because it saves time and effort. For cotton, I will manage it more carefully on a smaller area, with a little more potassium and more pest control, because that crop is more sensitive. My main goal this year is stable output, manageable work, and lower risk.
